title: JVM build egress allowlist
$comment: MIRRORED, not applied. bin/lib/egress-conf.mjs is the gate that actually runs — it throws on an empty allow[], a non-string host, and a host that would swallow the list; bin/test/jvm-egress.test.mjs additionally fails an entry with no `why`. This schema documents the shape those checks enforce. Required fields are taken from the VALIDATOR, not from the current three entries, so it does not over-fit today's data.

denyLogIsEvidence.description: How a refused connection is recorded. A denial nobody logs is indistinguishable from a request never made.

tiers.description: What each tier MEANS, written down beside the entries that claim one. Added 2026-08-27 when a non-registry host had to become reachable: services.gradle.org 307-redirects the gradle distribution to github.com and then to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, so the lane could not bootstrap at all without them. Two tiers rather than one because 'reachable' had stopped being a single idea — an artifact registry serving immutable versioned artifacts and a release CDN serving whatever the release contains are not the same permission, and collapsing them is how an allowlist widens without anybody deciding to widen it.

allow.$comment: Empty is refused: a proxy started from an empty allowlist permits nothing and is a control nobody can state the shape of.

host.description: A hostname, optionally dot-prefixed for subdomain matching. Lowercase is enforced because the reader compares literally: an uppercase entry would never match, and a never-matching allow entry reads as permission granted while granting nothing.

why.description: What needs this host and what it is. The length floor is deliberate — 'needed' is not a reason, and one-word justifications are how an allowlist stops being reviewable.

tier.description: OMITTED means green: an artifact registry, reachable on its own terms. `amber` means the host is reachable ONLY because the specific artifacts fetched from it are pinned by hash elsewhere and that pin is enforced by the thing doing the fetching — today, manifests/gradle-distributions.json and the distributionSha256Sum bin/jvm-resolve.sh injects. `red` is not a value here: red is the default and lives in `deliberatelyAbsent` or in nothing at all. An amber entry whose reason names no enforcing pin is a green entry wearing a warning label, which is worse than either, and bin/test/egress-conf.test.mjs asserts against exactly that.

deliberatelyAbsent.$comment: Hosts considered and refused, kept so a later reader sees the decision rather than an absence.
